title: First-tier Tribunal LON/00AG/BUM/2025/0001: appeal against a Building Safety Regulator decision on a regularisation certificate for works near a public sewer
jurisdiction: England (UK): Secretary of State determination / appeal / tribunal under the Building Act 1984 and Building Regulations; comparative test only, not Alberta
code_edition: Building Regulations 2010 (as amended): Requirements A1/A2 (structure), H1 and H4 (drainage, building over sewers); regulation 18A and s.18A(5)

facts.text: The case is an appeal against a Building Safety Regulator decision under section 18A(5) of the Building Regulations 2010 about a regularisation certificate.
facts.locator: cover page; decision section (docx text line 40)

facts.text: The decision of 2 December 2025 is corrected under the slip rule on 9 December 2025.
The works include a side extension, loft conversion and refurbishment project.
The local authority's decision recorded that the works did not comply with standards A1, H1 and H4.

The reasons recorded in the decision state that the foundations are close to the public sewer with their underside above the sewer invert, and that drainage details (bedding, backfill, proximity to the pipe) are insufficient.
The Building Safety Regulator's summary of outcome: appeal upheld in respect of requirement A2 and refused in respect of requirements H1 and H4.
The Thames Water build-over agreement provided relates only to proximity to the public sewer and does not confirm compliance with building regulations, according to the reasons summary.
The tribunal records that the regulator's best evidence was that it was 'not sure' whether H1 and H4 were complied with, and that there is no finding that there is a breach of those standards.

Decision: the regulator's decision of 14 August 2025 is varied; the appeal from the local authority's decision of 21 June 2025 is upheld; the decision is varied to grant the required regularisation certificate.
